items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The owner, M. Bonnevalle, also ran a movie house in another town and he was a nice man to work for.

ctx.x: The owner of the Cave du Majestic had another place called the Palais d'Eté, not far from the Cave, which resembled a large beer hall. In fact they served more beer than any other drink. Alchohol is not served in most cafes and dance halls in Belgium. This place had two bandstands and engaged attractions. We had to play afternoon tea dances and I disliked that, because we had to play on a bandstand that was in the window near the entrance. There was quite a large terrace with tables, where people could have…

The owner, M. Bonnevalle, also ran a movie house in another town and he was a nice man to work for. As I said before, no alchohol was sold in his place, I mean like cognac or whisky, the strongest thing was vermouth or beer. But there was a liquor store on a street just behind the cave and I had a pint bottle which I would take there and get me juice from a barrel.
Everything went along smoothly until the end of June, and we had been playing every afternoon and night since the 15th that month. Then we found out that the boss didn't have a working permit for us.
